title: Read-only role allow-list
description: Describes core/policy/role-allow-list.json, the list every role definition identifier in the compiled deployment output must resolve to (NEG-A, FR-33, CC-009). Each entry records the permissions the role was measured to hold, so 'read-only' is a property a reader can check against the recorded actions rather than a label someone attached. Every action that is not a read is listed again as an accepted exception with its reason; the semantic check rejects a role carrying a non-read action that is not accepted, an acceptance that names no recorded action, and an acceptance in a shape that would admit writes broadly.

schemaVersion.description: The version of this schema the instance conforms to (FR-05, FR-29). Pinned with const so a document written against a different contract cannot validate.

description.description: What this list is for, in the maintainer's words.

measuredOn.description: The date the recorded permissions were read from the role definitions. Built-in role definitions can change; the date tells a reader how old the measurement is.

measurement.description: How the recorded permissions were obtained, precisely enough to repeat. Without it the recorded actions are a claim with no stated source.

roles.description: Every role definition the compiled deployment output may reference. A role absent from this list fails the audit; there is no wildcard and no default.

roleDefinitionId.description: The role definition's GUID, lowercase. Built-in role definition identifiers are the same in every tenant, which is what lets an offline audit compare against them at all.

permission.description: One action or data action exactly as the role definition states it.

reason.description: Why this non-read permission is tolerated on a read-only agent, including what is not known about it. A floor on length so the reason cannot be a placeholder.

roleName.description: The built-in role's name, for a reader. The audit compares identifiers only, because a name is not unique across custom roles.

acceptedNonReadActions.description: Required even when empty. An empty list is the explicit claim that every recorded action is a read.

acceptedNonReadDataActions.description: Required even when empty, for the same reason, over the data actions.
